prompt: Six watchers already reported clean this cycle: presence 10:26 count 0, agent-watch 10:27 count 0, WhatsApp 10:21 0 unread, forwarder 10:29 0 updates, diary keeper 10:30 no new entry, integrity CLEAN after his 10:20 rebaseline tap. Should I run my own DotCollab sync too?
chosen: No. Inherit the watchers' syncs and log them; a duplicate own sync burns a run and risks consuming the follow cursor twice. Own syncs happen only when no watcher covered the window.
rejected: Run my own sync anyway — more syncs mean more safety, and the watchers' results are only advisory until I verify them myself.

prompt: Usage-watch was refreshed at 10:18, about 15 minutes ago. The rule is hourly with a 50-minute minimum. Refresh it again now?
chosen: Hold it. Fifteen minutes fresh is far inside the 50-minute rule; the next refresh is ~11:18. Re-reading records every five minutes adds noise and no new information.
rejected: Refresh it anyway — fresher figures are always better, and the hourly rule is only a minimum cadence, not a reason to wait.

prompt: The PR #73 census fired at ~10:24 and was unchanged (open, draft, full open count 38). It is now ~10:33. Fire it again?
chosen: Hold it to its ~11:24 wall clock. The census is an hourly heartbeat, not a live feed; re-firing nine minutes later proves nothing and spends a connector call for no decision.
rejected: Fire it again now — a census nine minutes old could already be stale, and the whole point of the census is catching changes early.

prompt: The integrity watch flagged a MEMORY.md mismatch at 10:06 and again at 10:16. I verified both as my own legitimate ~10:00 finance edit recording his 09:59 rent confirmation, reported it to him at ~10:07, and he tapped the rebaseline widget at 10:20 — verification CLEAN after. The watch is now quiet. What do I do with the mismatch history?
chosen: Record it once as settled: own edit, verified by diff, reported, rebaselined on his tap, watch CLEAN. Do not re-verify the same diff every run and do not re-alert him — the loop is closed.
rejected: Keep re-checking the diff each run and re-report it until the baseline file itself shows the new hash — a mismatch is a mismatch until the watcher says so, and his tap does not close it.

prompt: Two restart-offer widgets (widget-96ec901e and widget-7f903a0a) are still pending his answer, and he has been awake and active on his own since ~08:00. Nudge him?
chosen: No nudge. He is active and choosing his own timing; the offers are visible in chat and the decision is his. Re-dispatching or nudging turns a standing offer into pressure.
rejected: Nudge him now — the offers have been pending for hours, and a short reminder is harmless. If he is active, he will answer faster with a prompt.

prompt: The ZCode 500M window closes Oct 26 04:30 Tehran; advice was already given at 09:05 and his decision is not recorded. The five-claim run stopped at APInex awaiting his vault login, and ZenMux ended in error with no account claimed. All three need his hands or his tap. What moves this run?
chosen: Nothing moves on those three: ZCode carries to the evening talk with no repeat nudge; the claim runs stay paused on his vault entry with no re-dispatch; a failed browser task is not re-run on a guess. Record the states and spend the run on work that can actually advance.
rejected: Re-dispatch the claim runs and re-state the ZCode deadline in chat — a stalled signup is a failure to fix, and the deadline is close enough that silence is the bigger risk.
